Graft missing clades on a time-calibrated phylogeny

Source: R/graft_missing_clades.R
graft_missing_clades.Rd

This function grafts missing taxa onto an ultrametric, time-calibrated backbone phylogeny as clades sister to clades of the backbone. Missing taxa sharing the same sister clade are grafted together as one missing clade, on the stem branch of their sister clade.

The divergence time of the missing clade is drawn from a birth-death model fitted on the sister clade, and the missing clade is grown under the same model, conditioned on its number of taxa and its stem age.

Usage

graft_missing_clades(
  phy,
  missing_taxa_list,
  min_tips = 5,
  return_BD_model_summary = FALSE,
  total_richness_per_clades = NULL,
  simmap = NULL,
  allowed_states = NULL,
  treat_states_as_ranges = FALSE,
  return_simmap = TRUE,
  min_valid_fraction = 0.1,
  max_age_redraws = 1000,
  seed = 1234,
  nb_simulations = 1,
  force_simulations = FALSE,
  parallel = NULL,
  save_temp = FALSE,
  save_temp_every = NULL,
  temp_file_path = NULL,
  clean_temp_files = TRUE,
  resume = FALSE,
  ultrametric_tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.5,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

phy

An object of class "phylo". The backbone phylogeny on which taxa are grafted. It must be rooted, binary (no polytomies) and ultrametric (i.e., be time-calibrated). It can be the output of a previous grafting: the grafted tips then accumulate (see 'Successive graftings').

missing_taxa_list

A list with the information on the taxa to graft. Every item provided must be named after $Taxon_name. Items:

  • $Taxon_name: Character vector of the names of the taxa to graft. Names must be unique and absent from phy$tip.label.

  • $Sister_clade: List (named after $Taxon_name) of character vectors. For each taxon, the tip labels defining the sister clade, i.e., the clade of the backbone that is sister to the missing clade. Taxa with the same sister clade are grafted together as one missing clade. A pair of tips defines the clade as their MRCA node. A single tip defines the "clade" as the terminal branch of this tip. Clades must be defined by tips: node IDs are not accepted (the function stops, and lists some of them). Use phylograftR::convert_nodes_to_tips() to convert node IDs into pairs of tips.

  • $Sister_clade_name: (Optional) Character vector (named after $Taxon_name) of the names of the sister clades (NA if a clade has no name). Taxa sharing the same sister clade must have the same name. The names are not used for the grafting, but, if total_richness_per_clades is provided, they are checked against its $Sister_clade_name (a clade must have the same name in both objects).

  • $allowed_states: (Optional) List (named after $Taxon_name) of character vectors. For each taxon, the states of the simmap in which its missing clade can be grafted on the stem branch of its sister clade. It overrides the global argument allowed_states for this taxon. NULL or NA use the global argument. Only used with a simmap. Taxa with the same sister clade are grafted together as one missing clade, so they must have the same allowed states (the function stops otherwise, and lists the clades concerned). With the maps of several traits, each element is a list with the states of each trait (NULL: no taxon-level value for the trait), e.g., list(M1 = list(c("blue", "green"), "high"), M2 = list(NULL, "low")) (see 'Several traits' in Details section).

min_tips

Integer. Minimum number of tips of the clade used to fit the birth-death model. If the sister clade has fewer tips, the smallest enclosing clade with at least min_tips tips is used instead. Must be at least 3. Default is 5.

return_BD_model_summary

Logical. Whether to report the birth-death models fitted during the grafting. If TRUE, each grafted phylogeny has the attribute "BD_model_summary": a data.frame with one row per model (i.e., per missing clade), summarizing diversification rates and sampling fraction. It can be extracted a posteriori with phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary(). Default is FALSE.

total_richness_per_clades

(Optional) List with the total number of species of the clades, to account for species that are neither in the backbone nor in missing_taxa_list (i.e., unsampled species) when fitting the birth-death models. Items:

  • $Sister_clade: List of character vectors of tips, defining clades as in missing_taxa_list$Sister_clade. Node IDs are not accepted: convert them with phylograftR::convert_nodes_to_tips() in the same call as missing_taxa_list, so the tips of the clades match between both objects. The easiest way to obtain this list is to build it from a table of clades with phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades() or phylograftR::import_total_richness_per_clades(): the clades can be written with names, tips or node IDs, they are matched with the clades of missing_taxa_list, and the richness is checked against all the taxa to graft. It must cover all the unique sister clades of missing_taxa_list. It can include other clades, e.g., enclosing clades.

  • $Sister_clade_name: (Optional) Character vector of the names of the clades, same length as $Sister_clade (NA if a clade has no name). The names must be unique. If missing_taxa_list$Sister_clade_name is provided, a clade must have the same name in both objects (the function stops otherwise). They are not used for the grafting, but they are reported by phylograftR::extract_sampling_info().

  • $total_richness: Vector of positive integers, same length as $Sister_clade. Total number of species of each clade, i.e., backbone species, missing species nested within the clade, and unsampled species. Use NA if unknown: the unsampled species are then assumed to be those of the clades with an informed total richness nested within the clade (none if there are no such clades).

With NULL (default), missing species to graft and backbone species are assumed to cover all species in the focal group (no unsampled species). If the list is provided with only NA in $total_richness, the fits are identical (no unsampled species in any clade, total_richness = backbone + missing species).

To obtain a posteriori the species richness and the effective sampling fraction of the clades in each grafted phylogeny, use phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() on the output, with the same total_richness_per_clades.

See 'Sampling fraction and unsampled species' in Details section.

simmap

(Optional) A stochastic character map of the backbone, of class "simmap" (e.g., from phytools::make.simmap() or phytools::sim.history()), or a set of maps of the same trait, of class "multiSimmap" (e.g., from phytools::make.simmap(nsim = 10)), used as alternative hypotheses of the evolution of a species attribute (e.g., a trait or a range) with discrete states along the branches of phy.

Alternatively, you can provide a list of "simmap" and/or "multiSimmap" objects, one per trait, that contains the maps of several traits used together as constraints All maps must have the same tips, topology and branch lengths as phy. With a simmap, the missing clades can only be grafted on the parts of the stem branches of their sister clades that are in their allowed states (see allowed_states), and each missing clade inherits the state(s) of the point of the stem branch where it is grafted, along all its branches, so the states can be followed alongside the phylogeny.

See 'Species attributes', 'Multiple stochastic maps' and 'Several traits' in Details section. Default is NULL (no restriction for grafting based on states).

allowed_states

Character vector. The states of simmap in which grafting is allowed. This is the default for all taxa: taxa with a value in missing_taxa_list$allowed_states use this specific value instead. States are matched exactly with the states of the simmap, unless treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE. Taxa with no allowed states (neither a global nor a taxon-level value) can be grafted in all the states of the simmap. The function stops if some states are not in the simmap, or if allowed_states is provided without a simmap. With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, a range that is not a state of the simmap is accepted if it is contained in some of them (e.g., "A" can be allowed if "AB" is found on the simmap).

With the maps of several traits (a list in simmap), you must provide a list with one element per trait, in the order of the traits or named after them. In each element, the states allowed for each trait are named, with NULL for no restriction on a trait, e.g., list(c("blue", "green"), NULL, "high") (see 'Several traits' in Details section). Default is NULL (all states allowed).

treat_states_as_ranges

Logical. Only used with a simmap. Whether the states of the simmap are biogeographic ranges to be treated as sets of areas, rather than as unrelated states. Ranges must be coded as in BioGeoBEARS: one capital letter per area, and the letters of a multi-area range in alphabetical order (e.g., "A", "AB", "ABC"). If TRUE, an allowed range enables grafting on branch pieces in any range that contains it: "A" can be grafted on "A", "AB" and "ABC", whereas "AB" can be grafted on "AB" and "ABC" but not "A".

If stochastic maps of several traits are provided (a list in simmap), you must provide a logical vector with one value per trait, with at most one TRUE to define the trait treated as biogeographic ranges, the other traits being matched exactly. The vector is positional (e.g., c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE): the second trait is the range trait) or named after the traits, in any order (e.g., c(biogeo = TRUE, color = FALSE, elevation = FALSE)). A single FALSE is accepted with several traits (no range trait), but a single TRUE stops.

See 'Biogeographic ranges as states' and 'Several traits' in Details section. Default is FALSE (states are matched exactly).

return_simmap

Logical. Only used with a simmap, and silently ignored without it. Whether to add the updated simmap to the output, in $simmap (see 'Value'). Default is TRUE.

min_valid_fraction

Numeric between 0 and 1. Only used with a simmap. Threshold of the fraction of the time window of the divergence time of a missing clade (the stem branch of its sister clade) that is in its allowed states. A warning lists the missing clades below the threshold for inspection, as their divergence times are concentrated on a small part of the stem branch. The fraction is computed on the backbone, before grafting. Default is 0.1.

max_age_redraws

Integer. Only used with a simmap. Maximum number of times the divergence time of a missing clade can be drawn again when it falls in a part of the stem branch that is not in an allowed state. The function stops with an informative message if this limit is reached. Default is 1000.

seed

Integer. Seed used for reproducibility. The seed only applies within the function: the state of the random number generator of the R session is restored on exit. Set to NULL to use the random number generator of the session. Default is 1234. With several simulations, it is the master seed: the first simulation uses seed, and the seeds of the other simulations are derived from it (see 'Multiple simulations').

nb_simulations

Integer. Number of simulations, i.e., of grafted phylogenies to produce in the same run, from the same backbone and missing_taxa_list. The grafting is stochastic, so ideally downstream analyses should be run on a set of grafted phylogenies rather than on a single one. Default is 1. See 'Multiple simulations' in Details section for handling of the output, the seeds and the failures.

force_simulations

Logical. Whether to try new seeds until nb_simulations grafted phylogenies are obtained, up to 10 * nb_simulations attempts (see 'Multiple simulations' in Details section). If FALSE, the simulations that fail are skipped. Default is FALSE.

parallel

Logical or NULL. Whether to run the simulations in parallel, with the packages future and future.apply (they must be installed separately from phylograftR). Default is NULL: the simulations are run in parallel if the user set a future plan with several workers beforehand (e.g., future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)), and sequentially otherwise. FALSE forces a sequential run, even if a plan is set. TRUE execute the future plan, but stops with an informative error if the packages are not installed or no plan is set. See 'Parallel computation' in Details section for recommendations on whether parallelization is useful in your case.

save_temp

Logical. Whether to save the grafted phylogenies during the process, to recover from a crash or an interruption of long runs (see 'Temporary saves and resuming' in the Details section). Each phylogeny (one per simulation and per stochastic map) has its own temporary file. Its progress is saved every save_temp_every missing clades, and the phylogeny is always saved once fully grafted. Default is FALSE.

save_temp_every

Integer or NULL. Frequency of the saves of the progress, in number of missing clades grafted (groups of taxa with the same sister clade). Only used if save_temp = TRUE. Default is NULL: save each phylogeny only once fully grafted.

temp_file_path

Character string. Path of the .rds file used for the temporary saves. It must end with .rds and its directory must exist and be writable. Default is NULL, which saves in "temp_phy_from_grafting.rds" in the working directory. With several simulations and/or several stochastic maps, the path is a template: the suffixes "_map_<name>" (several maps; "map_" is not repeated if the name of the map already starts with it, e.g., "temp_map_1.rds" for a map named "map_1") and "_sim_<k>" (several simulations) are added before ".rds", in this order (e.g., "temp_map_A_sim_2.rds"). See 'Temporary saves and resuming' in the Details section.

clean_temp_files

Logical. Whether to delete all the temporary files of the run once it is completed without stopping/crashing. Only used if save_temp = TRUE. If the run crashes or is interrupted, nothing is deleted so it can be resumed. Use FALSE to keep the files. Default is TRUE.

resume

Logical. Whether to resume an interrupted run from its temporary files, which must come from a run with the exact same arguments (see 'Temporary saves and resuming'). Needs save_temp = TRUE. Default is FALSE.

ultrametric_tol

Numeric. Tolerance used by ape::is.ultrametric() for the ultrametricity checks of the backbone and of the final phylogeny. Default is .Machine$double.eps^0.5.

verbose

Logical. Whether to display progress. Messages print every 10 missing clades. If computation is run in parallel, only a message is printed when each simulation is done. Default is TRUE.

Value

The function returns an object of class "phylo": the backbone phylogeny with the grafted taxa added as new tips. Backbone branch lengths are untouched, and the grafted phylogeny is ultrametric.

In addition to the standard elements of a "phylo" object, the phylogeny has the following elements:

  • grafted_tips Named logical vector with one value per tip, in the order of $tip.label. TRUE for grafted tips (including the tips grafted by a previous grafting if phy was already grafted). Names are the tip labels.

  • grafted_edges Named logical vector with one value per branch, in the order of the rows of $edge. TRUE for grafted branches, i.e., branches with only grafted taxa descending from them. Names are the IDs of the tipward nodes of the branches ($edge[, 2]). Use them to color the phylogeny on plots (see examples).

These elements are not updated by functions that modify the phylogeny (e.g., ape::drop.tip(), which removes tips but keeps the other elements as they are, and ape::write.tree(), which removes them). Use phylograftR::identify_grafted() to recompute grafted_tips and grafted_edges on a manipulated phylogeny.

Optional elements can be added to the output based on what optional argument was provided:

  • "BD_model_summary" (attribute). Only if return_BD_model_summary = TRUE. Data.frame with one row per birth-death model fitted (one per missing clade), summarizing information about the clade used for model fitting, diversification rates, and sampling fraction. It can be extracted a posteriori with phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary().

  • simmap Only if a simmap is provided and return_simmap = TRUE. The updated stochastic character map of the grafted phylogeny (class "simmap"): the pieces of the branches of the backbone keep their states (cut where taxa were grafted), and every grafted clades is entirely in the state of the point where it was grafted. With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, each grafted clade is entirely in the range it inherited (see 'Biogeographic ranges as states' in Details section). This element can be plotted as any simmap, e.g., plot(grafted_phy$simmap), or used to extract the states of the tips with phytools::getStates(grafted_phy$simmap, type = "tips"). It has the same exact topology and branch lengths as the grafted phylogeny. With the maps of several traits, $simmap is a list of such simmaps, one per trait, named after the traits (see 'Several traits' in Details section).

With nb_simulations > 1, the function returns an object of class "multiPhylo" with one grafted phylogeny per simulation, named "sim_1", "sim_2", ... Each phylogeny has the elements described above (including $simmap if a simmap was provided and return_simmap = TRUE). The "multiPhylo" object has the attributes "seeds" (named vector of the seeds of the phylogenies, to reproduce each of them alone with nb_simulations = 1; NULL if seed = NULL) and "failed" (data.frame with the seed and the reason of the simulations that failed, 0 row if none).

With multiple stochastic maps (i.e., a "multiSimmap") provided as simmap, the function returns a list with one element per map (named after the maps): a phylogeny if nb_simulations = 1, a "multiPhylo" otherwise (see 'Multiple stochastic maps'). The list has the attribute "failed_maps" (data.frame with the map and the reason of the maps without any simulation, dropped from the output). The phylogenies have the attributes "seed" (their seed, unless seed = NULL) and, with several maps, "map", to ensure reproducibility of each simulation.

Details

Stop conditions

The function stops, before any grafting, if the backbone is not ultrametric, or if a sister clade is the whole tree (it has no stem branch to graft on).

Grafting process

Groups of missing taxa sharing the same sister clade are ordered by the size of the sister clade, so nested sister clades are processed first. For each group:

  1. A birth-death model is fitted with phytools::fit.bd() on the sister clade, or on the smallest enclosing clade with at least min_tips tips. The model is fitted on the crown group of this clade, with the sampling fraction of this crown group (see Sampling fraction and unsampled species).

  2. The divergence time of the missing clade is drawn on the stem branch of the sister clade with TreeSim::corsim(): between the crown age of the sister clade and its stem age (or between the present and the stem age for a single-tip sister clade).

  3. A single missing taxon is grafted as a new tip at this divergence time. For several taxa, a missing clade is grown with TreeSim::sim.bd.taxa.age() under the fitted model, conditioned on the number of taxa and on its stem age (the drawn divergence time), and grafted on the stem branch of the sister clade.

Unlike graft_missing_taxa(), this function has no "uniform" method: a birth-death model is always required. It is needed to generate the subtree of the missing clade under a diversification process. The model is fitted on the sister clade (or its enclosing clade), and used to produce the subtree to be grafted, conditioned on the number of taxa and its divergence time. Additionally, the fitted model is used to draw the divergence time of the missing clade on the stem branch of its sister clade.

Enclosing clades

When a sister clade contains fewer tips than min_tips, an alternative higher clade is selected to fit the birth-death model. This 'enclosing clade' is identified by walking rootward the tree node by node, starting from the sister clade, until a clade meets the min_tips condition. This ensures that the diversification dynamics modeled are based on enough tips to be relevant, while being closely associated with the sister clade.

Sampling fraction

The birth-death model is fitted on the crown group of the sister clade or its enclosing clade, so the sampling fraction is: n_present / (n_present + n_pending + n_unsampled), with n_present the tips of the fitted clade in the current tree (backbone tips and taxa already grafted, so missing clades grafted in nested sister clades processed earlier are not missing anymore), n_pending the taxa of missing_taxa_list still to graft whose sister clade is strictly nested within the fitted clade, and n_unsampled the unsampled species derived from total_richness_per_clades (0 without it).

Taxa that are sister to the fitted clade itself are outside of its crown group, so they are not counted: when the sister clade itself is fitted (i.e. have at least min_tips tips) and nothing is pending nor unsampled within it, the sampling fraction is 1. When an enclosing clade is fitted, the taxa to graft on the sister clade (nested in the enclosing clade) are counted. The divergence time of each missing clade is still drawn with TreeSim::corsim(missing = 1): unsampled species only influence the fitted rates, they do not take a branch.

Unsampled species

For a focal clade with a total_richness value provided: nb_unsampled = total_richness - nb_backbone - nb_missing, with nb_missing the number of taxa to graft as missing clades within the focal clade (because their sister clade is nested within the focal clade), therefore to be included in this focal clade during grafting. For a clade with no total_richness value (NA, or enclosing a sister clade without being listed), nb_unsampled is the sum of nb_unsampled over the largest clades nested within it with a total_richness value provided. If there is none, nb_unsampled = 0. The rationale is that even if nb_unsampled cannot be derived from its total_richness (as it is not provided for this clade), it has to at least account for the nb_unsampled species that have being identified in its own nested clades.

If total_richness_per_clades = NULL, nb_unsampled = 0: the clades have no unsampled species (the same as providing only NA in $total_richness).

Each missing clade is grafted on the stem branch of its sister clade in all the grafted phylogenies: only the divergence times vary among simulations and maps. The species present in each listed sister clade, and the resulting sampling fractions for downstream analyses, are therefore the same in all the grafted phylogenies. Use phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() to extract them a posteriori.

The function stops, before any grafting, if total_richness_per_clades does not cover all the sister clades, if a total_richness provided is lower than the number of backbone species plus missing species of the clade, or if a clade has fewer unsampled species than the sum of the clades with an informed total_richness nested within it.

Species attributes: allowed states of a simmap

A simmap describes the states of a discrete attribute (e.g., a trait or a range) along the branches of the backbone: each branch is cut in pieces, each piece being in one state. Missing clades are grafted on the stem branch of a clade of the backbone, and the function assumes that the user considers this stem branch a valid place for them. Restricting the grafting to some states of the stem branch is therefore only useful when the user has a strong hypothesis about a change of state along the stem branch that should affect where the missing clade can be grafted. For most uses, the simmap is not needed.

For example, in biogeography: a stem fossil is found in range A, and the sister clade is in range A, while the missing clade is in range B. If the shift from range B to range A on the stem branch of the sister clade is estimated to have occurred before the age of the fossil, the missing clade can be restricted to the part of the stem branch before the shift, with allowed_states = "B".

With a simmap, a missing clade is only grafted on the pieces of the stem branch of its sister clade that are in its allowed states (missing_taxa_list$allowed_states of its taxa if provided, otherwise the global argument allowed_states). The divergence time of the missing clade is drawn with TreeSim::corsim() as without a simmap: if it falls in a part of the stem branch that is not in an allowed state, it is drawn again, up to max_age_redraws times.

The simmap can also be provided so that the states are updated alongside the phylogeny: the whole missing clade (all its taxa and branches) inherits the state of the point of the stem branch where it is grafted. The updated simmap is returned in $simmap, if return_simmap = TRUE). The allowed states are not required: without any allowed states, all the states are allowed, grafting is not restricted by the states, but the simmap will be updated, assuming grafted clades inherit the state of the point where they are grafted.

The function stops, before any grafting, if the taxa of a same missing clade have different allowed states, or if the stem branch of a sister clade has no piece in the allowed states (the clades are listed), and warns about the missing clades with a small share of their stem branch in allowed states (see min_valid_fraction).

Cautions for interpretation: risks of circularity.

Constraining the grafting by a trait that will then be analyzed (e.g., the association of the trait with diversification) may bias the results towards the constraint. The grafted taxa are placed only where the trait allows it, so they are in the allowed states by construction. This can create or inflate an association between the trait and the diversification dynamics, affect the rates of transitions between states, or inflate the phylogenetic signal of the trait. It also reduces the uncertainty about the state of the grafted clades since they always inherit a unique state. It is recommended to acknowledge these potential biases when interpreting such analyses.

To limit the risk of circularity, multiple approaches are possible:

  • constrain the grafting by traits that are not the object of downstream analysis;

  • compare the results with and without the constraint (or on the backbone only);

  • keep the constraint as loose as the information allows (e.g., allowed states that include neighboring states);

  • use several maps and simulations to propagate the uncertainty in ancestral state estimates.

Biogeographic ranges as states

With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, the states of the simmap are biogeographic ranges, coded as in BioGeoBEARS (one capital letter per area, and the letters of a multi-area range in alphabetical order, e.g., "AB"), and the allowed states are the ranges a missing clade can have.

An allowed range matches a state of the simmap if it is contained in it: a missing clade allowed in "A" can be grafted on the parts of the stem branch in "A", "AB" or "ABC", whereas a missing clade allowed in "AB" only can be grafted on the parts of the stem branch in "AB" or "ABC".

When multiple allowed states are provided, the inherited range is drawn randomly from the allowed ranges enclosed within the range of the stem branch piece where it is grafted. When grafting on an edge with a larger range than the inherited range (e.g., "A" on "AB"), this results in a subset sympatric speciation event such as (AB) -> (AB), (A). In the returned simmap, the branches of the grafted clades are in their inherited range, whereas the stem branch it is grafted on continues in its own range.

Multiple simulations

With nb_simulations > 1, the grafting is simulated nb_simulations times from the same backbone and the same missing_taxa_list. Each simulation starts again from the backbone: the birth-death models are fitted on the tree of the simulation (they depend on the taxa already grafted), and the simulations do not share anything but the inputs. The phylogenies are returned in a "multiPhylo" object (a single "phylo" if nb_simulations = 1), and the memory used grows with the number of simulations.

The first simulation uses seed, so it is the same phylogeny as a run with nb_simulations = 1 and the same seed. The seeds of the other simulations are drawn from a stream started by seed, and returned in the attribute "seeds": a simulation can be reproduced alone with its seed, and the first simulations of a longer run are the same as the ones of a shorter run. With seed = NULL, the simulations follow the random number generator of the session.

A failure that is specific to a simulation, because of the random draws (no usable divergence age or time after max_age_redraws redraws), skips this simulation with a warning: the name of a phylogeny keeps the index of its simulation (e.g., "sim_3" is missing if the third simulation failed). The function reports the number of phylogenies obtained if it differs from nb_simulations, and stops if no simulation succeeded. With force_simulations = TRUE, new seeds are tried until nb_simulations phylogenies are obtained (up to 10 * nb_simulations attempts): the phylogenies are then named "sim_1" to "sim_N" without gaps, and the seeds of the failed attempts are in the attribute "failed". Any other error (invalid inputs, no branch available for a taxon, ...) concerns all the simulations and stops the whole run.

With save_temp = TRUE, each simulation saves its own temporary file (see 'Temporary saves and resuming').

Multiple stochastic maps

When multiple stochastic maps of the same trait are provided as a "multiSimmap", the grafting is run with each of its maps. The maps are alternative hypotheses of the evolution of the same trait (or range), used as alternative constraints. All the maps and the simulations are crossed: each map is used for nb_simulations simulations, so P maps give P * nb_simulations grafted phylogenies. This can lead to a quick inflation of computation time, thus a warning is sent if the total number of grafted phylogenies (P * nb_simulations) is more than 1000.

The output is a list with one element per stochastic map, named after the maps (the names of the "multiSimmap" if it has some, otherwise "map_1", ..., "map_P"). With nb_simulations = 1, each element is a grafted phylogeny. With several simulations, each element is a "multiPhylo" (see 'Multiple simulations') with phylogenies named "<map>_sim_1", "<map>_sim_2", ... and the attributes "seeds" and "failed" of the map. Each phylogeny can be reproduced alone with its map (as a single simmap) and its seed.

A map for which no simulation could be obtained is dropped from the output with a warning, and listed in the attribute "failed_maps" of the list (data.frame with the columns map and reason). The function stops if no map gives any phylogeny.

With save_temp = TRUE, each map and each simulation saves its own temporary file (see 'Temporary saves and resuming').

Several traits

The maps of several traits can be used at once to constrain grafting. simmap is then a list with one element per trait, each a "simmap" or a "multiSimmap" (e.g., simmap = list(color = color_simmap, elevation = elevation_simmap)). The elements can be named after the traits (with different names that cannot contain ;, ,, = or |), otherwise the traits are named "trait_1", "trait_2", ... All the maps must have the same tips, topology and branch lengths as the backbone phy.

A taxon can only be grafted on the parts of the branches that are in one of its allowed states, for every trait. The allowed states are provided for each trait, in the order of the list of maps (or named after the traits): the global argument allowed_states is a list with one element per trait, e.g., list(c("blue", "green"), NULL, "high") for three traits, and missing_taxa_list$allowed_states has such a list for each taxon. A trait with NULL (or an empty vector, or NA) has no taxon-level value, so the global allowed_states of the trait is used for the taxon (a taxon-level value replaces the global one, trait by trait, as with a single trait). A trait with no states, neither at the taxon level nor globally, has all its states allowed (no restriction). Other traits can still be restricted: list(NULL, "high") only restricts the second trait.

With return_simmap = TRUE, $simmap is a list of updated simmaps, one per trait, named after the traits. In each simmap, a grafted branch is entirely in the state of each trait at the point where it was grafted (each trait is inherited from the lineage it was grafted on).

With a list of "multiSimmap" provided as simmap, the maps of the traits are paired: the grafting is run with the map 1 of every trait, then the map 2 of every trait, and so on. All the traits must therefore have the same number of maps to be associated in a given grafting process.

One of the traits can be treated as biogeographic ranges combined with any number of other traits. Use a logical vector in treat_states_as_rangesto define which of the trait is to be treated as biogeographic ranges for inheritance. The range logic is the one of 'Biogeographic ranges as states' for the range trait: its allowed values for grafting are any ranges that encompass the allowed range. For instance, a missing clade allowed in "A;high" can be grafted on stem branch pieces in "A;high", "AB;high" or "ABC;high", whereas a missing clade allowed in "AB;high" only can be grafted on stem branch pieces in "AB;high" or "ABC;high".

The other traits are matched exactly, and are inherited as they are from the point where the clade is grafted: with "AB" and "high" at the graft point and the allowed range "A", the whole missing clade inherits "A" and "high". Only one trait can be treated as ranges to prevent inflation of the number of combined allowed states to consider.

Parallel computation

The simulations based on the different stochastic maps and seeds are independent, so they can be run in parallel with the package future and future.apply. Both packages must be installed independently from phylograftR.

The grafting function does not manage the workers: you must set a plan beforehand, e.g., future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4), and reset it afterwards with future::plan(future::sequential). With the default parallel = NULL, the function uses the plan if there is one, parallel = FALSE ignores it. All the P * nb_simulations simulations (with P stochastic maps per trait) are run as one set of tasks, so the workers are used evenly.

The output is exactly the same as without parallelization. The messages, warnings and printed output of the simulations are relayed to the session when the tasks are collected (so they appear after the simulations, not live), and with verbose = TRUE one line is printed when each simulation is done.

Setting up the workers and sending the data to them has a time cost, so parallelization only pays off with large backbone phylogenies, or many simulations or maps. As a rule of thumb, use parallel computation when the sequential run would last more than a minute or so, i.e., for large backbone phylogenies (500 tips or more) and several grafted phylogenies (nb_maps * nb_simulations), or for 50 or more grafted phylogenies on small backbones.

Temporary saves and resuming

With save_temp = TRUE, each grafted phylogeny (one per simulation and per stochastic map) is saved in its own .rds file, built from temp_file_path by adding the suffixes "_map_<name>" when a "multiSimmap" is used, then "_sim_<k>" when nb_simulations > 1. For instance, with temp_file_path = "dir/temp.rds":

  • a single phylogeny uses "dir/temp.rds";

  • several simulations use "dir/temp_sim_1.rds", "dir/temp_sim_2.rds", ...;

  • several maps use "dir/temp_map_A.rds", "dir/temp_map_B.rds", ...;

  • several simulations across several maps use both suffixes as "dir/temp_map_A_sim_1.rds";

  • the prefix "map_" is not repeated if the name of the map already starts with it: maps named "map_1", "map_2", ... (default names of a "multiSimmap" without names) use "dir/temp_map_1_sim_1.rds", "dir/temp_map_2_sim_1.rds", ...

With force_simulations = TRUE, <k> is the number of the attempt, not necessarily the ID to which the grafted phylogeny will be attributed to in the final output. This is required to identify the appropriate seed used to produce each attempt; attempts that failed leave a file too for tractability.

Temporary files can be read with readRDS() and used to plot the grafted phylogeny in its current state. The object is a regular "phylo" with the attribute "phylograftR_temp" that stores what is needed to resume a run. Once the phylogeny is fully grafted, the file is replaced by the complete output of the simulation (with $simmap, $grafted_tips, etc.).

With clean_temp_files = TRUE (default), all the temporary files of the run are deleted once the function returns without crashing. A run that crashes or is interrupted never deletes its files, so it can be resumed with resume = TRUE. Use clean_temp_files = FALSE to keep the files after a successful run.

With resume = TRUE, the function must be called again with exactly the same arguments as the interrupted run. For each phylogeny, its temporary file is searched: a complete phylogeny is reused as it is, an unfinished one is continued from its last save, and a phylogeny without file is grafted from scratch.

Resuming is not equivalent to grafting the taxa left on the temporary phylogeny used as a new backbone, with a missing_taxa_list restricted to these taxa: the taxa already grafted would be treated as backbone species, so the sampling fractions of the birth-death models, the stem of the target clades, the identification of the grafted tips and the updated simmap would be wrong, and a simmap of the initial backbone would not match the temporary phylogeny. Use resume = TRUE instead.

Successive graftings

To graft the missing taxa and the missing clades on the same backbone, use graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(), which chains both steps with a single set of inputs and a single seed, including with several simulations and/or stochastic maps.

The output of this function can also be used as the phy of another grafting (e.g., to chain the steps by hand for a single grafted phylogeny).

The grafted tips and branches accumulate: if phy has the grafted_tips element of a previous grafting, its flagged tips are kept as grafted (they are still treated as backbone species by the grafting itself, e.g., to count the species used for the sampling fractions), and the new taxa are added to them. grafted_tips and grafted_edges of the output thus identify all the grafted taxa, not only those of the last step. A warning is sent if grafted_tips does not match the tips of phy (e.g., after ape::drop.tip()): use identify_grafted() to recompute them first.

If a simmap is used, provide the updated simmap of the previous step (phy$simmap, obtained with return_simmap = TRUE) to keep the same trait history.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() to build a missing_taxa_list from a data.frame loaded in R, with clades defined by tips or node IDs.

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy() to build a missing_taxa_list from taxonomic tables, with clades defined by taxonomic names.

  • phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades() and phylograftR::import_total_richness_per_clades() to prepare total_richness_per_clades for the unsampled species.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades() to graft missing taxa and missing clades in one run, with a single set of inputs.

  • phylograftR::check_grafting_plan() to check a priori the feasibility of a grafting plan, before grafting.

  • phylograftR::check_grafting_constraints() to check a posteriori that grafted taxa respect their constraints.

  • phylograftR::extract_grafting_info() to extract a posteriori information on the location of grafted lineages.

  • phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() to extract a posteriori the richness and the sampling fraction of the clades in each grafted phylogeny.

  • phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary() to extract a posteriori information on the birth-death models fitted during grafting (with return_BD_model_summary = TRUE).

  • phylograftR::plot_grafted() to plot grafted phylogenies.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# --- Prepare data --- #

# Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units
set.seed(1234)
phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30)
phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50

# List the missing taxa to graft
missing_clades_list <- list(
  Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4"),
  # Sister_clade is named after Taxon_name (same names, same order)
  # M1 and M2 share the same sister clade: they are grafted together as one missing clade
  Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = c("t8", "t22"), M3 = c("t26", "t18"), M4 = "t5"))

# --- Perform grafting --- #

# Graft the missing clades
grafted_phy <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                    verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)
plot(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)


# Highlight the grafted tips and branches in red
plot_grafted(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)



# --- Produce several grafted phylogenies --- #

# The grafting is stochastic: several simulations can be run at once from the same backbone and list
# (a "multiPhylo" named sim_1, sim_2, ...; sim_1 is the same as a single run with the same seed)
grafted_phys <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                      nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)
names(grafted_phys)
#> [1] "sim_1" "sim_2" "sim_3"
# Seeds of the simulations, to reproduce each phylogeny alone
attr(grafted_phys, "seeds")
#>     sim_1     sim_2     sim_3 
#>      1234 488349520 469344150 

# Plot phylos
old_par <- par()["mfrow"]
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 1, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #1") # sim_1
plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 2, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #2") # sim_2
plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 3, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #3") # sim_3

par(old_par)


# --- Account for unsampled species --- #

# Account for unsampled species with the total richness of the sister clades.
# All the unique sister clades must be listed (NA = unknown richness)
total_richness_per_clades <- list(
  Sister_clade = list(c("t8", "t22"), c("t26", "t18"), "t5"),
  total_richness = c(20, NA, 3))
grafted_phy_richness <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                             total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades,
                                             verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Inspect the resulting clade richness and sampling fractions
extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_phy_richness,
                      total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades)
#>    map simulation seed Clade_tips total_richness total_richness_provided
#> 1 <NA>          1 1234    t8, t22             20                    TRUE
#> 2 <NA>          1 1234   t26, t18             17                   FALSE
#> 3 <NA>          1 1234         t5              3                    TRUE
#>   nb_backbone_species nb_grafted_species nb_unsampled_species sampling_fraction
#> 1                  13                  1                    6         0.7000000
#> 2                  17                  0                    0         1.0000000
#> 3                   1                  0                    2         0.3333333


# --- Apply attribute-based exclusions --- #

# Restrict the grafting to some states of a stochastic character map (simmap) of the backbone
# The toy simmap has three states, "blue", "green" and "red"
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_simmap)

# List the missing taxa to graft
missing_clades_list <- list(
   Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"),
   Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t26", "t18"), M2 = c("t26", "t18"), M3 = c("t26", "t18"),
                       M4 = "t14", M5 = "t14"))

# The simmap shows that the targeted stem branches recorded state shifts.
plot(toy_simmap, col = c("blue" = "dodgerblue", "green" = "limegreen", "red" = "firebrick"))


# We can use 'allowed_states' to limit grafting on the "green" portions of the stem branches
   # The stem branch from the "bottom" clade shifts from "green" to "red"
   # The terminal (stem) branch of "t14" shift from "green" to "red" too
grafted_phy_states <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,
                                           missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                           simmap = toy_simmap, allowed_states = "green",
                                           verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Plot output phylogeny with colored grafts
plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states, use_simmap = FALSE, cex = 0.7)


# The updated simmap is in the output: the new grafted clades branch from the "green" segments
# of the stem branches of their sister clades, and each newly grafted clades are entirely "green"
# Grafted branches are dashed lines, and grafted tips are labelled in red.
plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states,
             simmap_colors = c("blue" = "dodgerblue", "green" = "limegreen", "red" = "firebrick"))



# --- Use several stochastic maps (alternative hypotheses of trait evolution) as constraints --- #

# A 'multiSimmap' gives several stochastic maps of the same trait:
# the grafting is run with each of them.
# Here, 3 maps are simulated from the states of the tips of the toy simmap.
tip_states <- phytools::getStates(toy_simmap, type = "tips")

# (the random number generator of the session is restored afterwards)
had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
set.seed(118)
toy_multiSimmap <- phytools::make.simmap(toy_backbone, tip_states,
                                         model = "ER", nsim = 3, message = FALSE)
if (had_seed)
{ assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
} else { rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) }

# Graft using constraints from all 3 simmaps X 2 simulations per simmap
grafted_phys_maps <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,
                                         missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                         simmap = toy_multiSimmap, allowed_states = "green",
                                         nb_simulations = 2, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Inspect output:
# A list with one element per simmap, each a multiPhylo with the simulations of the map
names(grafted_phys_maps)
#> [1] "map_1" "map_2" "map_3"
names(grafted_phys_maps$map_2)
#> [1] "map_2_sim_1" "map_2_sim_2"
# The map and the seed of a phylogeny are included as attributes for reproducibility
attr(grafted_phys_maps$map_2[[1]], "map")
#> [1] "map_2"
attr(grafted_phys_maps$map_2[[1]], "seed")
#> [1] 1234


# --- Constraints from several traits at once --- #

# Load the simmap for the second trait: 'toy_simmap_elevation' has two states: "high" and "low".
data(toy_simmap_elevation)

# Provide the maps of the traits as a list
# The global 'allowed_states' has one element per trait (here, "green" color and "low" elevation).
grafted_phy_traits <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,
                                           missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                           simmap = list(color = toy_simmap,
                                                         elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),
                                           allowed_states = list("green", "low"),
                                           verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# '$simmap' is a list of updated simmaps, one per trait
names(grafted_phy_traits$simmap)
#> [1] "color"     "elevation"

# Newly grafted clades can only be grafted on and harbor the allowed state in each trait
plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 1) # Only 'green'

plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 2) # Only 'low'



# --- Constraints from biogeographic ranges and another trait at once --- #

# One of the traits can be treated as biogeographic ranges:
# the allowed ranges do not have to match exactly the range of target stem branch pieces,
# any allowed range comprised in a target range is valid (e.g., "A" can be grafted on "AB").
# Here, the first trait holds ranges.

# Load the range simmap
data(toy_simmap_ranges)

# The clades are grafted on stem branch pieces in ranges
# containing "A" or "B" and in elevation "low"
grafted_phy_ranges_traits <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
    simmap = list(biogeo = toy_simmap_ranges, elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),
    allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), "low"),
    treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE),
    verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# '$simmap' is a list of updated simmaps, one per trait: ranges, and elevation
names(grafted_phy_ranges_traits$simmap)
#> [1] "biogeo"    "elevation"

# Newly grafted clades can only harbor the allowed state/range in each trait
# They can be grafted on range that encompasses their allowed range (here, "AB")

# Range: Grafted on "A", "B", or "AB", but inherit only "A" or "B".
plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 1)

# Elevation: Only 'low'
plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 2)
